title: G2 Intent Data Alternatives
summary: A breakdown of some G2 alternatives for intent data.
body_text: G2 Buyer Intent captures first-party behavioral signals from inside the G2 marketplace; someone viewing your product profile, comparing you to a competitor, or checking your pricing page. It rolls that activity into account-level Buying Stage and Activity Level scores that flow into CRM and ABM tools like Salesforce and HubSpot. Quick take: Strength: high-fidelity, first-party signal - someone comparing you to a named competitor on G2 is a much stronger indicator than inferred third-party topic interest. Limits: it's account-level (no contact name), G2-only (nothing outside the marketplace), and a data feed rather than a full platform — no built-in enrichment or outreach. Pricing: not public; teams typically report $20K–$60K/year depending on category coverage. That narrowness is why most GTM teams look at G2 alongside - or instead of - other options. Here's how the main alternatives compare. 4 G2 Alternatives 1. Letterdrop Letterdrop's flagship product today is Competitor Monitoring: identifying named contacts who are actively starting sales cycles with your competitors, so reps can intercept deals before they're lost. It's contact-level rather than account-level data. It reports roughly 30% accuracy for correlating a signal with a live competitor sales cycle, which the company positions as the closest thing to visibility into a competitor's pipeline without access to their CRM. Beyond competitor signals, Letterdrop pulls from a broader mix than most providers: Standard buying-intent signals Non-standard public sources: government filings, RFPs, job postings, OSHA/FDA records Social listening across public conversations for buyers discussing relevant problems Champion job changes and closed/lost deal revival, mined from a company's own CRM notes, calls, and email history Every signal is matched against your ICP, enriched into a named contact, and delivered with a drafted outreach message. It integrates with Salesforce, HubSpot, Slack, Clay, and existing sales engagement platforms, so leads land where reps already work. See who your competitors are talking to 2. Bombora Best feature: the broadest topic coverage in the category, pulling intent from a co-op of over 17,000 B2B publishers - strong for early-funnel, category-wide visibility. It's third-party and topic-level, so you're seeing who's reading about a topic, not who's comparing vendors. Company names arrive with no contacts attached, so enrichment is still a separate step. 3. 6sense Best feature: enterprise-grade predictive scoring layered on third-party intent, website de-anonymization, and full ABM orchestration - advertising, sequencing, and deep Salesforce-native workflows in one platform. Six-figure contracts are standard, and teams under a few hundred employees often find it more than they can operationalize - without the headcount to act on the intelligence, you've paid for a dashboard nobody works. 4. ZoomInfo Intent Best feature: consolidation. It layers Bombora's topic data on top of ZoomInfo's own contact database and first-party "Scoops" (hiring, funding, and initiative triggers), so intent and contacts live in one login. The topic intent underneath is Bombora's, not a unique source, and it's gated behind a ZoomInfo contract - not something you can buy standalone at a lower price point. Which one should you use? Already active on G2 and investing in a listing? G2 Buyer Intent is a reasonable, high-fidelity add-on. Need broader third-party coverage? Bombora or ZoomInfo fit better. Running genuine enterprise ABM with budget and headcount to match? 6sense is built for that. Want fewer dashboards and more contact-level leads reps can act on same-day? That's the gap Letterdrop closes - and the only option here that skips a separate enrichment step entirely. Know when a competitor is talking to your prospects. Letterdrop surfaces contacts in active conversations with your competitors and routes them to your reps before the deal closes. See it in action

title: Sign-Up Form Best Practices to Push Submit Rates Past 3% - Klaviyo
summary: Get sign-up form best practices from a year of real Klaviyo account audits, covering incentives, timing, and A/B tests that push submit rates past 3%.
body_text: Sign-up form best practices: what a year of audits taught me Generated by Klaviyo AI Maria Trotta, Senior Digital Strategist on Klaviyo's Professional Services team, draws on a year of auditing Klaviyo accounts (plus 12 years running lifecycle and retention at DTC brands) to break down why most sign-up forms underperform and what separates the ones that convert. The piece uses real brand examples — Bearpaw, MERIT Beauty, Caden Lane, Tata Harper, Leonisa, and minnow — to walk through benchmarks, common failure points, and a testing framework for improving submit rates. Submit rates should beat the 3% floor: Klaviyo's general benchmark is a 3% submit rate, but Trotta calls that a low bar — she's seen brands hit 8–20%. Expected ranges vary by form type: standard pop-ups run 3–8%, while exit-intent and phone-only forms tend to land at 10–13%. Weak incentives and generic copy tank performance: Low submit rates usually come down to a form that isn't giving people a reason to care — common culprits include generic non-branded copy, identical email and SMS messaging, poor mobile optimization, weak copy hierarchy, and no creative investment. Converting forms share four traits: Across her audits, high-performing forms consistently include an eye-catching headline, a clear incentive, a real value proposition, and compliance copy that reads with personality rather than fine print — as seen in examples like MERIT Beauty's pop-up, which pairs a product image with a concise "ships free" offer. Sign up Get a demo When was the last time you looked at your sign-up form? If you can't remember, you're not alone. Many of the brands I work with haven’t updated their sign-up form in years. But when you neglect your front door, you lose curb appeal and no one wants to visit. And that means you miss out on valuable relationships. When each new subscriber is a potential customer, that’s a lot of revenue potential to leave up to one outdated form. I've spent the last year auditing Klaviyo accounts across dozens of brands. Before that, I spent 12 years running lifecycle and retention as a team of one at DTC beauty and lifestyle brands. I've seen a lot of forms. Most of them are fine. But “fine” is the problem. What's a good sign-up form submit rate? While Klaviyo sets the general benchmark submit rate at 3% , I would say that’s a low bar. I’ve worked with brands with submit rates in the 8–20% range. If you’re under 3%, it’s time to re-evaluate your strategy. If you’re at 3%, you should still be working on it. Where your form lands in that range depends a lot on what kind of form it is and who it's targeting. Here’s what I’d expect to see: Standard pop-up form (first touch on your homepage): 3–8% Exit-intent forms: 10–13% Phone number capture-only forms: 10–13%, especially when targeted at email subscribers The more targeted it is, the better the sign-up form tends to perform. A standard “Sign up for our newsletter” pop-up asks a stranger for a lot with very little context. An exit-intent form or a phone number-specific ask, shown to someone who's already engaged, is more likely to convert. Footwear brand Bearpaw runs a bigger incentive on their exit pop-up than on their welcome pop-up, perhaps based on the theory that someone who’s about to leave needs a stronger reason to stay. Their exit pop-up submit rate now sits at 2.7x the median of their 100 closest peers. Source: Bearpaw Why is my sign-up form underperforming? Low submit rates usually trace back to one of two things: a weak incentive, or a form that just isn't giving people a reason to care. Sign-up forms need to offer something of value that gives the customer a reason to hand over a personal piece of information. Most customers don't even redeem the welcome code, but the sheer fact that they got something makes it feel like a fair exchange. In other words, the incentive signals the relationship is a two-way street. Free shipping, early access, an exclusive text message-only drop, a small discount: any of these can work, as long as there's a clear “Here's what you get” attached to “Here's what I'm asking for.” Sometimes, retention teams have trouble getting sign-up forms approved at all. Creative teams often see pop-ups or forms with discounts as beneath the brand, and I understand the sentiment. Nobody wants their site to feel like a discount outlet. But the assumption that a well-designed pop-up form is inherently spammy or tacky is really just a hypothesis. And hypotheses can be tested. Your customers probably like certain sign-up form elements more than you do. Personally, I’m not super into a spin to win. But I used it with a brand, and it earned a 20% sign-up rate. So what if I don't love it? Our audience did. As a marketer, your job is to design your sign-up form to follow your brand guidelines, and always listen to what your audience wants. At the end of the day, think, “Do I want customers or not?” Other reasons for sign-up form underperformance are fairly consistent across brands: Generic, non-branded copy: If your form copy could belong to any brand, it's not doing its job. Identical copy for email and text messaging: These are two different lists and very different asks when it comes to a customer’s attention. Poor mobile optimization: 53% of consumers make retail or ecommerce purchases on mobile, according to Klaviyo’s 2025 Future of Consumer Marketing Report . Assume the majority of traffic will come from mobile and that your form design needs to be mobile-first. This is non-negotiable. Weak copy hierarchy: If you're offering a discount, that offer needs to be the first thing someone sees. Don’t bury it under 3 lines of brand narrative. No creative investment: A block of solid color with white text and no images technically counts as a form, but it probably won’t convert. Treat a pop-up form as seriously as any other piece of brand marketing. If leadership decides against a pop-up form, that’s their call to make. But go back to your goals, and run experiments to see where your highest-value customers are coming from. If it’s your pop-up, it may be worth re-evaluating. What’s the anatomy of a sign-up form that actually converts? Across the audits I've run, the forms that consistently perform well share 4 things: An eye-catching headline: Use copy that stops users in their tracks. A clear incentive: Include a discount or product offer rather than just asking someone to join a list. A real value proposition: Explain why someone should want to receive your emails or text messages. Compliance done right: Include consent language that names your company, has personality, and doesn't read like fine print. MERIT Beauty's sign-up pop-up form includes a product image, a clear incentive (“Ships free with every first order”), and compliance copy that’s concise and noticeable. Source: MERIT Beauty Using your sign-up forms as personalization engines Conventional wisdom says fewer form fields means higher conversion, but that's not universal. Baby clothing brand Caden Lane tested 30 versions of their sign-up form and found the opposite: their conversion rate was highest when the form asked for more context, not less, including who the shopper was buying for. The extra fields let Caden Lane personalize every future message to every subscriber, and shoppers responded well to that trade-off. Source: Caden Lane Using AI to optimize your sign-up forms AI forms display optimization can refine your pop-up timing, creative, and audience rules, testing variations automatically and serving the best-performing version to each visitor. Skincare brand Tata Harper , for example, saw a 65% increase in sign-up form submissions after using forms display optimization on two forms, all without having to run manual tests. Source: Tata Harper When and where should my sign-up form appear? People spend a lot of time debating pop-up vs. slide-in vs. full-screen. In my experience, that's not the most important conversation, especially when mobile forms take up the full screen anyway. What’s more important are your form settings: the time delay, your target audience, form frequency, and page exclusions. Here are a few things to keep in mind: Pair a time delay with a scroll trigger, rather than showing the form immediately on page load. Something like a 5-second delay combined with a 20% scroll gives people a chance to orient themselves before you ask for anything. Exclude pages where a form doesn't belong. Your check-out and about pages are two obvious destinations to exclude your sign-up forms from. Don't skip the teaser. If someone closes your form on first load and there's no way back in, that subscriber is gone for good. A teaser module gives them an easy way to get back to signing up when they’re ready. Some brands really don’t want to use the teaser, which is okay. But in that case, I’d recommend having delays across your website to make sure you're not losing people the second they land on the page. Based on my experience, skipping the teaser will cost you. Text message-specific forms have different challenges and considerations. Asking someone to type a full phone number and confirm consent with a one-time code is a bigger ask than dropping in an email address. With Klaviyo’s Smart Opt-in , subscribers can confirm their consent with autofill without leaving your site. Intimate apparel brand Leonisa targeted their text message sign-up prompts specifically to mobile shoppers, perhaps based on the logic that people already browsing on their phones would be the likeliest to opt in for mobile marketing. In the US, that targeting drove 1.6x the median form fill rate for Leonisa's peer group, according to Klaviyo benchmarks. How can I set up a testing program for my sign-up forms? Klaviyo's AI-powered forms display optimization is a useful way to find the best form timing and settings. To get a clear dataset, run these tests during times that are business as usual, not during busy sale periods and launches. The instinct to test during a high-traffic moment, like a sale or a product launch, makes sense on the surface: more traffic should mean more data. But the behavior underneath that traffic isn't the same. Somebody is probably going to sign up during a sale or a launch because it's new and exciting, and the offer is usually better than what you'd show on a regular day. So that test isn't telling you what your baseline form performance actually is. The better approach is to build a full picture over time: a baseline test during a quiet period, plus separate tests during your bigger moments, so you know what actually works in each context rather than assuming one setting fits every scenario. Important notes: Whichever test you run, give it enough time to reach statistical significance . Let it accumulate at least a few hundred submits per variation before calling a winner, and resist the urge to check the results daily. Early leads flip more often than you'd think. Always change only the variable you’re testing. For example, if you’re testing incentive type, make sure you keep headline, copy, images, timing, and structure the same, so you can be sure it’s the variable you’re testing that causes any differences. With that in mind, here are some example A/B tests you can run: Incentive type (e.g., percentage off vs. dollar amount vs. free shipping) Different incentives can be worth roughly the same to the customer but perform very differently on the form. For example: A: “Get 15% off your first order.” B: “Free shipping on your first order, always on us.” Incentive amount (e.g., 10% vs. 15%) Find the smallest offer that still converts, so you're not giving away margin the form doesn't need. For example: A: “Unlock 10% off your first order.” B: “Unlock 15% off your first order.” Headline copy (e.g., offer-first vs. brand-first) Test an offer against a line in your brand voice, and let the submit rate settle the internal debate. For example: A: “Get 15% off your first order.” B: “Your best skin starts here” (and move the offer to the subhead). Imagery (e.g., product shot vs. lifestyle shot vs. no image) A form with strong imagery often beats a text-only version more than any copy tweak would. But you can prove it with a test. For example: A: form with a product image on a clean background B: the same form with a photo featuring a customer using the product C: the same form, no image at all Timing (e.g., immediate vs. a 5-second delay paired with a 20% scroll trigger) This is to test audience settings and timing. For example: A: form fires on page load B: form fires after a 5-second delay and 20% scroll depth Form structure (e.g., single-step vs. multi-step) Test whether your audience is willing to fill out more form fields or not. If they are, you can send more targeted messages in the future. Gauge success based on both submit rate and what that extra field can do for personalization. For example: A: one screen asking for email address only B: two screens, where the first screen asks for email address, and the second asks a question like, “Who are you shopping for?” In this example from apparel brand minnow , the first step of the form asks the subscriber who they’re shopping for. The form features a lifestyle image along with their brand colors, their logo, and a large headline with the 15%-off promotion. Source: Minnow Teaser status (e.g., on vs. off) If your team is skeptical of the teaser, this test settles the argument with your own data instead of someone else's best practice. For example: A: The teaser tab stays docked at the bottom of the screen after someone closes the form. B: No teaser, and the form is gone once closed. How often should I redesign my sign-up forms? Revisit your forms on a schedule, not just when something breaks. Put it on the calendar. I recommend brands revisit their forms at least once a quarter. If you're running a sitewide sale, your sign-up form needs to match that offer. But you’ll also have to update everything downstream: your sign-up form, welcome flow, and abandoned cart messaging should all show the same promotion or discount, messaging, and branding. Your ongoing sign-up form update schedule could look something like: Quarterly baseline refresh, even if it's just a new seasonal image and a copy pass BFCM and major sitewide sales, with messaging that matches your flows Product launches, where a form update can double as a teaser for what's coming Early-access moments, for brands with loyalty programs or VIP tiers If it's been more than a quarter since anyone looked at your sign-up form, it’s been too long. Review for sharper copy, add real incentives, make sure design is mobile-first, and set the timing so people have room to actually notice the offer before you ask for their information. Turn your sign-up forms into a growth channel with Klaviyo Get everything you need to audit, test, and rebuild your forms lives in one place with Klaviyo. The autonomous B2C CRM makes it easy to test your strategy again and again, with: Centralized subscriber data in unified customer profiles , essential for 1:1 personalization at scale Sign-up forms that come with built-in targeting rules, A/B testing, and AI forms display optimization, so you can test your way to better submit rates Smart Opt-in for text message marketing , which lets subscribers confirm consent with autofill so they don’t have to go to their messages to find a code Try Klaviyo Maria Trotta Maria is a seasoned digital marketing leader with 10 years of experience driving retention and growth for direct-to-consumer brands through email, SMS, and integrated lifecycle marketing. She specializes in turning customer insights into scalable digital strategies that improve engagement, conversion, and long-term value. As a senior SMS digital strategist at Klaviyo, Maria partners with brands—from fast-growing challengers to household names—to optimize their messaging strategies and unlock stronger performance across the customer journey. Her work focuses on aligning data, personalization, and channel strategy to deliver measurable results. title: SEAWORLD TO BRING HORROR FRANCHISE “I KNOW WHAT YOU DID LAST SUMMER” TO HOWL-O-SCREAM THIS FALL
body_text: Buy Now and Save During Limited-Time Sale to Experience the All-New Haunted Houses Inspired by Sony Pictures’ “I Know What You Did Last Summer: The Final Catch” at SeaWorld Orlando, San Diego and San Antonio as Part of This Year's Biggest and Most Immersive Howl-O-Scream Events ORLANDO, Fla., SAN DIEGO and SAN ANTONIO (July 31, 2026) – This fall, the past refuses to stay buried as SeaWorld Orlando, SeaWorld San Diego and SeaWorld San Antonio unveil all-new haunted houses inspired by the Sony Pictures horror movie, “ I Know What You Did Last Summer ,” marking the first time the film is being brought to life at a major Halloween event. Making its terrifying debut during this year's Howl-O-Scream events at all three parks, the immersive experience invites guests to step beyond the screen and into a nightmare where every secret has a price and every corner hides the vengeful Fisherman. The all-new haunted houses premiere on September 11 at all three parks. Based on the first installment of the iconic horror franchise licensed by Sony Pictures, “ I Know What You Did Last Summer: The Final Catch” is a haunted house version of the 1997 hit. Guests will wander through horrifying recreations of several unforgettable movie scenes and into the events that unfold during the original Southport massacre. The movie, and the haunted houses, tell the story of a group of friends who desperately attempt to hide a deadly accident, but their shared secret awakens a killer determined to make them pay. Now, SeaWorld guests will become part of that terrifying story. "We're always looking for new ways to raise the bar on immersive entertainment, and bringing ‘ I Know What You Did Last Summer’ to our Howl-O-Scream events is an exciting milestone for all three SeaWorld parks," said Marc Swanson, CEO of United Parks & Resorts. "This thrilling franchise has captivated horror fans for years with its suspense and terror. Now our guests will step into that world, facing some of the same heart-pounding moments that made the film come alive. As one thrilling part of a lineup of haunted houses, scare zones, live entertainment and immersive experiences, we are excited to deliver what we believe is our most ambitious Howl-O-Scream yet." The arrival of “ I Know What You Did Last Summer: The Final Catch” marks a major addition to SeaWorld's award-winning Howl-O-Scream events, where guests can experience elaborate haunted houses, immersive scare zones, sinister live entertainment, themed bars, and the most adrenaline-pumping coasters in the dark. Now is the perfect time to lock in the screams. At SeaWorld San Antonio, Howl-O-Scream is included with park admission, and guests can save on tickets, Season Passes and Annual Passes with the Summer Sale. title: Feriados e datas comemorativas de setembro: calendário do mês
summary: Descubra os principais feriados e datas comemorativas de setembro, com dicas práticas para aproveitá-las no seu negócio.
body_text: Setembro é um mês em que manter o caixa no verde exige estratégia em dobro para não deixar o estoque parado. Mas o lado positivo é que o calendário comercial oferece ganchos fortes de venda, como o Dia do Cliente . Essa é a oportunidade exata para resgatar quem já conhece seu trabalho, criar ofertas rápidas e garantir a receita. Neste guia, você confere os principais feriados e datas comemorativas de setembro . Salve as datas, alinhe a equipe e prepare a sua operação. Quais são os feriados de setembro? Setembro conta com apenas um feriado nacional: a Independência do Brasil , comemorada no dia 7 de setembro . Além da data nacional, consulte sempre o calendário da sua cidade e estado. Feriados regionais, como aniversários de municípios ou datas religiosas locais, alteram a rotina da região e são ótimos ganchos para ofertas segmentadas. 7 de setembro é feriado? Sim, o 7 de setembro é feriado nacional . A data celebra a Independência do Brasil e altera o expediente comercial em todo o país. Em 2026, o feriado cai em uma segunda-feira, criando o clássico feriadão prolongado. Para quem empreende, isso exige planejamento prévio. Se o seu negócio é de alimentação, turismo ou lazer, reforce o estoque e a equipe para o pico de movimento. 8 de setembro é feriado? A data não é um feriado nacional, mas é feriado municipal em capitais importantes como Curitiba (PR), Vitória (ES) e São Luís (MA) , que celebram suas padroeiras ou fundações. Se a sua loja fica nessas cidades, prepare-se para alterações no horário comercial. 15 de setembro é feriado? Não, o 15 de setembro não é feriado, mas para o varejo, ele vale ouro. É nesta data que comemoramos o Dia do Cliente , o principal evento comercial do mês. Como setembro não tem datas sazonais clássicas, essa é a sua chance de aquecer as vendas. 16 de setembro é feriado? Não no Brasil todo, mas é feriado estadual em Alagoas . O dia 16 de setembro marca a Emancipação Política do estado, paralisando serviços e alterando o funcionamento do comércio em todos os municípios alagoanos. 20 de setembro é feriado? Apenas no Rio Grande do Sul . O 20 de setembro é feriado estadual e celebra a Revolução Farroupilha, uma data com peso cultural gigantesco e que movimenta a economia local. Para os lojistas gaúchos, a Semana Farroupilha atrai eventos, turismo e engajamento. 22 de setembro é feriado? Não é feriado, mas a data marca o início da Primavera no Brasil . Para quem atua no varejo de moda, beleza, alimentação ou casa e decoração, a mudança de estação é o gatilho perfeito para girar os produtos na prateleira. Quais são as datas comemorativas de setembro? Confira as principais celebrações do mês que você pode aproveitar para realizar campanhas ou ações especiais no seu negócio. 01/09 – Dia do Profissional de Educação Física Se você atua no segmento de academias , moda fitness ou suplementação, pode criar parcerias locais ou oferecer descontos exclusivos para os profissionais que levarem alunos para comprar na sua loja. 05/09 – Dia do Irmão Essa é uma data com forte apelo emocional. Aproveite para girar o estoque criando ações promocionais do tipo “leve 2, pague 1” ou monte combos de brindes para compras em dupla, incentivando o cliente a marcar familiares nas redes sociais. 06/09 – Dia do Sexo Apesar de não ser uma data oficial, tem alto potencial de engajamento. É o momento ideal para marcas de bem-estar, moda íntima e produtos de autocuidado criarem campanhas ousadas e alavancarem as vendas. 09/09 – Dia do Administrador Empresas B2B, instituições de ensino e marcas voltadas ao público corporativo podem explorar a data para estreitar o relacionamento. É uma boa oportunidade para oferecer condições especiais em serviços focados na gestão de negócios. 15/09 – Dia do Cliente Essa é a alavanca de vendas mais importante do mês. É a oportunidade perfeita para oferecer descontos reais, queimar produtos parados e reforçar o relacionamento com seus consumidores. Confira ideias práticas para vender mais no Dia do Cliente 2026 21/09 – Dia da Árvore Com forte apelo ambiental, o Dia da Árvore é ideal para marcas que desejam reforçar seu compromisso com a sustentabilidade. title: HII Names Chris Helton as Vice President of Infrastructure and Sustainability at Newport News Shipbuilding
summary: HII is America's largest military shipbuilding company, delivering advanced warships, submarines, and mission technology solutions in service of the nation.
body_text: NEWPORT NEWS, Va., Aug. 3, 2026 — HII (NYSE: HII) announced today that Chris Helton has been appointed vice president of infrastructure and sustainability at its Newport News Shipbuilding division . In his new role, Helton will oversee infrastructure modernization improvements at the shipyard, as well as facilities, environmental health and safety, and security at NNS. He will report to Karey Malyszko , NNS vice president of quality, process excellence and plant operations. “Chris’ extensive educational background, strategic leadership and diverse shipbuilding experience will be critical to our success in making responsible investments that further power our drive to meet our commitments,” Malyszko said. A 35-year shipbuilder, Helton joins NNS from HII’s Ingalls Shipbuilding division , where he held positions of increasing responsibility across engineering, facilities, maintenance and planning. He played a critical role in Ingalls’ recovery from Hurricane Katrina in 2005, and he most recently served as director of post-launch electrical operations. Helton earned a bachelor’s degree in industrial engineering technology and a Master of Business Administration from the University of Southern Mississippi. He begins his new role at NNS Aug. 31.

title: Copy Collections
summary: You can now copy collections in Captain. One API call duplicates the documents, chunks, embeddings, and custom metadata under a new collection name, reusing the
body_text: Copy Collections You can now copy collections in Captain. One API call duplicates the documents, chunks, embeddings, and custom metadata under a new collection name, reusing the index you already built. bash 1 curl -X POST https://api.runcaptain.com/v2/collections/shipping_manuals/copy \ 2 -H "Authorization: Bearer $CAPTAIN_API_KEY" \ 3 -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 4 -d '{"target_name": "shipping_manuals_staging"}' Copied collections are fully independent. Writes and deletes stay scoped to the collection they were issued against. Why we built it Three requests kept coming up: One collection per customer. If you run retrieval for many end clients, each client's data belongs in its own collection: separate indexes and separate deletes. Standing up client number forty used to mean re-indexing a shared corpus for the fortieth time. Now you can index the base corpus once, then easily copy it per client. Staging copies. Sometimes a collection needs to branch. Production stays on the settings your users depend on while a copy absorbs the change you're not sure about yet: a different parsing configuration, a new chunk relationship setup, a different PII masking policy . Test against the copy with real data, and when the branch proves out, cut over. When it drifts too far, you can delete it and copy again. Experiments. Snapshot a collection before a risky change. If the experiment fails, delete the copy and the original is untouched. What it used to cost Before this endpoint, duplicating a collection meant re-indexing it from the source files: paying indexing credits on every document again, then waiting on the job queue, sometimes for hours, before the duplicate was usable. A copy is a flat 10 credits , billed once the copy succeeds. Because the vectors are copied rather than rebuilt, the operation completes in about a second . Both numbers hold at any collection size. Here it is against a real collection: POST /v2/collections/ :collection_name /copy Try it 1 curl -X POST https://api.runcaptain.com/v2/collections/blog_demo_shipping_manuals/copy \ 2 -H "Authorization: Bearer $CAPTAIN_API_KEY" \ 3 -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 4 -d '{"target_name": "blog_demo_shipping_manuals_staging"}' 200 Copied 1.28s 1 { 2 "success" : true , 3 "message" : "Copied 'blog_demo_shipping_manuals' to 'blog_demo_shipping_manuals_staging' (6 documents)" , 4 "source_collection" : "blog_demo_shipping_manuals" , 5 "collection_name" : "blog_demo_shipping_manuals_staging" , 6 "database_id" : "01a01749-7d73-7401-89ec-8261383d631c" , 7 "documents_copied" : 6 , 8 "files_copied" : 6 , 9 "namespaces_copied" : 1 10 } Details POST /v2/collections/{collection_name}/copy with a target_name in the body. The target name must be unused in the collection's environment; a taken name returns a 409. Copies land in the same environment as the source and behave like any other collection: query them, index into them, delete them. Reference documentation for the endpoint is at docs.captain.dev/reference/collections/copy . Lewis Polansky CEO & Co-Founder Aug 18, 2026

body_text: View all news Green Plains Reports Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results 08/06/2026 Download (opens in new window) PDF 203 KB Results for the Second Quarter of 2026: Net income attributable to Green Plains of $67.1 million, or EPS of $0.83 per diluted share Adjusted EBITDA of $93.3 million, inclusive of $34.6 million from the base business and $58.7 million in 45Z production tax credit value net of discounts and other costs Cash flow from operating activities of $86.3 million for the second quarter of 2026 The Superior, Iowa facility joined the Central City, Nebraska facility in achieving the Highly Protected Status from GPRE’s property insurance carrier, FM Lowered selling, general and administrative expenses by $5.9 million or 21% to $21.7 million for the second quarter of 2026 compared to the second quarter of 2025 88% utilization from the eight operating ethanol plants in the quarter OMAHA, Neb.--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Green Plains Inc. (NASDAQ:GPRE) (“Green Plains” or the “company”) today announced financial results for the second quarter of 2026. Net income attributable to the company was $67.1 million, or $0.83 per diluted share compared to net loss attributable to the company of $72.2 million or $(1.09) per diluted share, for the same period in 2025. Revenues were $446.2 million for the second quarter of 2026 compared with $552.8 million for the same period last year. Core operating profitability strengthened with adjusted EBITDA of $93.3 million compared to $16.4 million for the same period in the prior year. “The second quarter demonstrated the earnings capability of the Green Plains platform,” said Chris Osowski, President and Chief Executive Officer. “Even with lower utilization due to maintenance, we generated more than $67 million of net income. The combination of operational excellence, achieving multiple safety milestones, improved ethanol economics, strong commercial execution and our low-carbon platform is translating into meaningful financial results. ” “Our financial profile continues to improve as we execute on our operating and capital allocation priorities,” said Ann Reis, Chief Financial Officer. “Stronger earnings from our plants and continued discipline on SG&A are generating meaningful cash flow, which we intend to direct toward reducing debt and building a more resilient balance sheet that is positioned for growth.” Results of Operations Green Plains’ ethanol production segment sold 160.7 million gallons of ethanol during the second quarter of 2026, compared with 193.6 million gallons for the same period in 2025. The consolidated ethanol crush margin was $95.1 million for the second quarter of 2026, compared with $26.3 million for the same period in 2025. The consolidated ethanol crush margin is the ethanol production segment’s operating income before depreciation and amortization, including intercompany marketing and agribusiness fees and excluding net nonethanol operating activities. Consolidated revenues decreased $106.6 million for the three months ended June 30, 2026, compared with the same period in 2025, primarily due to lower revenues within our ethanol production segment as a result of lower volumes sold primarily driven by the disposition of our Obion, Tennessee plant. Net income attributable to Green Plains increased $139.4 million and adjusted EBITDA increased $76.9 million for the three months ended June 30, 2026 compared with the same period in 2025 primarily due to recognition of $58.7 million of 45Z production tax credits net of discounts and other costs, higher margins in our ethanol production and agribusiness and energy services segments and lower selling, general and administrative expenses as a result of restructuring costs of $2.5 million incurred during the three months ended June 30, 2025. Interest expense decreased $5.8 million for the three months ended June 30, 2026 compared with the same period in 2025 primarily due to prior year loan fees related to the issuance and modification of warrants in conjunction with access to a short-term line of credit and an amendment on our Junior Notes, offset by higher debt balances associated with carbon sequestration equipment. Income tax benefit was $5.5 million for the three months ended June 30, 2026, compared with income tax expense of $2.3 million for the same period in 2025 primarily due to the changes in the valuation allowance on deferred tax assets, offset by an increase in pre-tax book income from the generation of non-taxable 45Z production tax credits. During the first quarter of 2026, the company elected to early adopt ASU 2025-10, Accounting for Government Grants Received by Business Entities . Concurrently, the company elected to change its accounting policy related to the recognition of Section 45Z clean fuel production tax credits. The change in accounting policy results in the recognition of Section 45Z clean fuel production tax credits by analogy under the income model of ASU 2025-10, which results in a reduction of cost of goods sold in the statements of operations and recognition as production tax credits on the consolidated balance sheets. The company previously recorded the credits under ASC 740, Accounting for Income Taxes , which resulted in recognition within income tax benefit in the statements of operations and deferred income taxes, net in the consolidated balance sheets. The company determined that the income model under ASU 2025-10 is preferable because it better reflects the financial benefit of Section 45Z clean fuel production tax credits netted against the costs to produce the low-carbon fuels that the tax legislation was meant to incentivize. The company determined that retrospective adjustment to prior period financials is required. No Section 45Z clean fuel production tax credits were recognized during the first or second quarters of 2025, so no adjustments were made in the statements of operations; however, the company has reclassified balances previously reported as deferred income taxes, net, and other long-term liabilities to production tax credits on the consolidated balance sheets as of December 31, 2025. Segment Information The company reports the financial and operating performance for the following two operating segments: (1) ethanol production, which includes the production, storage, and transportation of ethanol, distillers grains, Ultra-High Protein, and renewable corn oil, in addition to CCS operations at our three Nebraska plants and (2) agribusiness and energy services, which includes grain handling and storage, commodity marketing and merchant trading for company-produced and third-party ethanol, distillers grains, renewable corn oil, natural gas and other commodities. title: GEMs ESG Materiality, H1 2026
summary: Data centres, AI and the electrification dividend
body_text: The Middle East conflict has prompted governments to re-assess their energy security and reduce exposure to hydrocarbon imports, encouraging the uptake of alternative energy sources. It has also spurred policy support for electrification which should boost a range of sectors, including electric vehicles (EVs), batteries and grid infrastructure. These shifts form part of a broader structural realignment driven by geopolitics, demographics, climate pressures and technological progress, and we believe companies able to respond to these challenges – while sustaining strong profitability and returns on equity – are well placed to outperform. Meanwhile, the huge sums of capital expenditure (capex) pouring into cloud service providers and data centres should significantly benefit emerging markets, driving further demand for semiconductors, while the knock-on benefits should boost companies providing solutions to ESG concerns (for example, energy demand and water scarcity) as well as manufacturers of servers, networking devices and other electronic components.

title: WMMR Legend Pierre Robert Named to the Radio Hall of Fame Class of 2026
summary: CHICAGO, IL – AUGUST 3, 2026 -- The Radio Hall of Fame announced today the selection of nine 2026 Legends inductees, including legendary WMMR-FM Philadelphia
body_text: CHICAGO, IL – AUGUST 3, 2026 — The Radio Hall of Fame announced today the selection of nine 2026 Legends inductees, including legendary WMMR-FM Philadelphia personality Pierre Robert. These individuals have received induction by the determination of the Radio Hall of Fame 2026 Nominating Committee, who annually meet to determine inductees who contributed with greatness to the radio industry and have since passed away. The Radio Hall of Fame is housed within the Museum of Broadcast Communications in Chicago. The following nine radio legends take their place in the Radio Hall of Fame immediately: Lin Brehmer- On-Air Personality Vivian Carter- On-Air Personality and Record Company Executive Dale Dorman- On-Air Personality Gary Krantz- Network Radio and Syndication Executive Wink Martindale- On-Air Personality, Game Show Host, and Television Producer Mitchell Reed- On-Air Personality Pierre Robert- On-Air Personality Polito Vega- On-Air Personality E. “Duke” Wright- Radio Station Owner and Executive Dennis Green, Co-Chair of the Radio Hall of Fame, said: “The Radio Hall of Fame is proud to honor this year’s Legends inductees, whose extraordinary careers have helped define the history and enduring impact of radio. From iconic on-air personalities to visionary executives, each has left an indelible mark on our industry and earned their rightful place in the Radio Hall of Fame.” Kraig Kitchin, Co-Chair of the Radio Hall of Fame, said: “It’s an honor and privilege to witness the induction of these radio industry legends. We hope this recognition of their industry contributions benefits their family, colleagues, friends and listeners.” The Radio Hall of Fame will recognize its 2026 class of inductees at the 2026 Radio Hall of Fame induction ceremony on Thursday, October 8, 2026, at the Fairmont Chicago, Millennium Park, 200 North Columbus Drive, Chicago, IL. Tickets are on sale now at: www.radiohalloffame.com . A portion of ticket purchases is a tax-deductible charitable donation to the Museum of Broadcast Communications. Fans and industry professionals can find more information, including photos and bios of the 2026 Legends, at www.radiohalloffame.com . The Radio Hall of Fame was founded by the Emerson Radio Corporation in 1988. The Museum of Broadcast Communications took over operations of the Hall in 1991. ABOUT THE MUSEUM OF BROADCAST COMMUNICATIONS The Museum of Broadcast Communications (MBC) collects, preserves, and presents historic and contemporary radio and television content as well as educates, informs, and entertains the public through its archives, public programs, screenings, exhibits, publications, and online access to its resources. MBC was founded in 1982 and is a 501(c)(3) registered non-profit entity. ABOUT THE RADIO HALL OF FAME The Radio Hall of Fame honors notable radio personalities and showcases their accomplishments in the Chicago-based Museum of Broadcast Communications. Each year, 24 nominations are determined by the organization’s Nominating Committee, which is comprised of industry leaders. A voting panel of industry members is invited to cast their confidential vote to determine inductees recognized annually.

title: Announcing Cloudflare Wallets: the programmable wallet for the agentic Internet
summary: Cloudflare Wallets will provide AI agents with native payments and verifiable identity on the web. Using the x402 protocol, agents can autonomously purchase APIs and content within clear safety guardrails.
body_text: Today, it is difficult for AI agents to try out new APIs. They often have to navigate through a login page designed for humans and not agents, contact a human to add a payment method, generate an API key, and then figure out how to call the API. This flow is very difficult for agents for two reasons: Agents do not have a stable identifier to sign up for an API, and they do not have a native way to pay for APIs. Because they lack these things, they often struggle to onboard onto software, which limits the growth of agentic commerce. AI agents often give up on these tasks entirely, kicking registration, payment methods, and API key generation back to humans. This makes it very difficult for agents to try out and compare many APIs. To solve this, we’ve created Cloudflare Wallets. Starting today, you can claim a Cloudflare Wallet handle for your account, which will provide a unique username to help you better connect with merchants. Soon, you will be able to set up and use your Cloudflare Wallet to pay for APIs and content. Earlier this month, we announced the Monetization Gateway to help Cloudflare customers get paid for their websites and applications. Monetization Gateway will support micropayments using the x402 protocol , which allows for payments to be attached to HTTP requests. These micropayments will be able to pay for uses ranging from AI inference to data to content. If you want to pay or get paid for services behind Monetization Gateway and other x402-compatible endpoints , you’ll need a wallet. Cloudflare Wallets will allow you to store stablecoins, purchase services, and receive funds across the web. Each account with a wallet will also be able to create Virtual Wallets for its agents to enable them to buy APIs, MCP Tools, content, and more. You will be able to define guardrails for your Virtual Wallets (such as an allowance, an allow list, and a maximum transaction size) to help your agent spend money safely from your account. This will allow your agent to try out many APIs with low friction and managed risk. Wallet users will have the option to share their Cloudflare Wallet handles, which will give them a stable identity when interacting with merchants. Building the two-sided agentic market Cloudflare’s Monetization Gateway will allow eligible Cloudflare customers to sell their resources (such as content or APIs) headlessly to agentic buyers. But for that market to truly develop, agents need more tools to buy from merchants in a machine-native way. Wallets will add another tool to Cloudflare’s Agents SDK, enabling AI agents to easily purchase necessary APIs and content using micropayments. There will be two types of Cloudflare Wallets: Account Wallets and Virtual Wallets. Account Wallets are designed for humans who are owners and users of Cloudflare accounts. They will be able to add funds, delegate spend to virtual wallets managed by agents, and remove funds as needed. Virtual Wallets , by contrast, are designed for agents and operate via API keys. Within a Virtual Wallet, an agent will be able to spend funds according to its permissions. Its maximum spend will be capped by the limit set by the owner of the Account Wallet. This framework gives agents freedom to act on behalf of users without constant manual approval while limiting an agent’s ability to overspend. The freedom to explore Virtual Wallets are exciting because they will allow agents to do what they’re best at: explore dozens or hundreds of services and find the best one for a particular use case. Stablecoin micropayments via x402 will make it simple to try an API without an account, allowing agents to test new options with little friction. The spending caps on Virtual Wallets are designed so that humans can let agents explore autonomously within safe spending limits. These limits may seem like constraints, but counterintuitively they give agents more freedom. If an agent is responsible for $10, you can worry less about its spending than if it is responsible for $1,000. If an API only costs a few cents to try, then $10 is more than sufficient to pursue and evaluate many options. Once you or your agent has picked an API to use, policies set by you in your Account Wallet will act as cost controls for Virtual Wallets. Want to give every employee a $100 per week budget for AI inference? Simply provision an Account Wallet with the right balance and create Virtual Wallets for each employee with that rule. Anyone who exceeds the limits on their Virtual Wallet will be able to request a manual override from a human who is authorized to make changes to the Account Wallet. We want to make it easy for Account Wallets to set flexible yet firm spending policies that do not require daily, active monitoring. When something anomalous happens, such as unexpectedly fast spending, a human will be able to review and confirm whether everything is operating as intended. If the spend was intentional, then the administrator of the Account Wallet will be able to raise the limit or approve a one-time injection of funds. If the spend was unintentional, then the spending policies for adding funds to virtual wallets did their job by imposing caps. We are working to make it as easy as possible to fund and use these wallets. We will start with simple ways to onramp and offramp funds within supported geographies, with self-funding via stablecoins available as an alternative for eligible users. The Internet will not shift completely overnight, but with a majority of traffic on the web now being driven by bots, we are excited to give agents and merchants first-class tools for agentic commerce. Beyond payments alone Allowing humans to delegate authority to agents to easily buy and sell services is a helpful starting point. But this delegation is not always obvious to the merchants as they interact with agents. Today, if an agent comes to your website, you may know little about them as a user, despite the fact that the agent is acting on behalf of an individual or an organization. This lack of attribution challenges many traditional web business models. It’s easy to give a one-week free trial or sign-up credits to a human or an organization. It’s hard to give these same perks to an agent that lacks a stable identity and when one human can spin up dozens of agents under their control. We solve this problem by linking wallets to a Cloudflare account via cloudflare.pay . cloudflare.pay will allow agents to optionally identify themselves, since their identity is a delegate of the account. A research agent could live at research.example.cloudflare.pay , allowing merchants to know that it is an agent from a particular organization. This approach will permit agents to maintain consistent and persistent identities, making the experience better for all parties. It will be completely optional for agents to choose to declare their identity or not, and it will be up to businesses to decide whether they want to prioritize transacting with known agents. Agent identifiers should be human-readable We believe that the approach to dealing with agents will look like the approach to dealing with VPNs: If someone is unidentified, they are not inherently untrustworthy, but they need to prove themselves more. This is why we have Turnstile and other initiatives to detect bots within Bot Management . Our identity primitive will build on top of this prior work. For example, Web Bot Auth already allows agents to register their identity via a keypair. IDs attached to Cloudflare Wallets allow this keypair to become human-readable. We know that agentic identity standards are changing quickly, which is why we wanted to keep our approach simple. We are proposing a human-readable identifier for a not-very-readable keypair, similar to the URL and IP-address pairings used in DNS . We are not trying to define a particular schema or other verification system. We only want to make identity simple to remember and easy to declare. As schemas to enrich agentic identity develop through the x402 Foundation’s initiatives, we will seek to adopt them and intend to encourage others to do the same. The future of agentic commerce At Cloudflare, we want to offer all the building blocks for agentic commerce to succeed. Monetization Gateway will offer a way for sellers to get paid without setting up traditional payment infrastructure. Wallets will offer a way for buyers to pay headlessly via agents. Identity will allow merchants to communicate with buyers who identify themselves or enforce identification requirements. All of these building blocks will create a headless marketplace for the Internet. If you are excited about this and want to participate, you can claim your handle now . We’re excited to see what you build and monetize.

title: Tuya Smart Launches Tuya AI Coding, Enabling Users to Build Their Own AI-Powered Lifestyle Apps with Natural Language
summary: /PRNewswire/ -- Tuya Smart (NYSE: TUYA; HKEX: 2391), a global AI cloud platform service provider, has officially launched Tuya AI Coding, an AI-native no-code...
body_text: HANGZHOU, China , Aug. 5, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Tuya Smart (NYSE: TUYA ; HKEX: 2391), a global AI cloud platform service provider, has officially launched Tuya AI Coding, an AI-native no-code application development platform enabling users to turn ideas into AI-powered lifestyle applications with just a single prompt. By describing their ideas, desired features, or interface requirements in natural language, users can generate applications that are runnable, deployable, and capable of powering real AI-driven experiences. The platform also supports one-click deployment and social media platform sharing. The launch of Tuya AI Coding marks a further step in Tuya's expansion from AI-generated pages to AI applications that can interact with the physical world, broadening the possibilities of the AI Home ecosystem. AI Application Development Is Moving Beyond Page Generation into Real Life Gartner has named AI-native application development platforms one of the top strategic technology trends for 2026, predicting that 75% of new applications worldwide will be built using low-code development approaches by year end. Behind this rapid market growth, a new industry shift is emerging: as the barrier to AI application development continues to fall, the standard for evaluating the value of these applications is also changing. Frost & Sullivan's July report noted that AI-native no-code app generation platforms are evolving from simply "creating apps through conversation" to "enabling complete business delivery," with competition now expanding beyond app generation capabilities to include deployment, launch, operations, and continuous iteration. In short, the "last mile" of AI application development is no longer just about generating code — it's about whether an application can integrate into real-world scenarios. An app confined to the browser, unable to interact with real services, devices, or data, has limited practical value. This is the challenge Tuya AI Coding was built to solve. Built to seamlessly connect human creativity with AI technology, the platform is designed to ensure that every AI-generated application is capable, from day one, of connecting with real devices, serving real users, and powering real-life experiences. Turning Ideas into AI Lifestyle Applications with a Single Prompt Most AI app generation tools on the market today remain limited to the digital world, stopping at the creation of web pages or mini-program interfaces. Built on Tuya's global AI+IoT technology stack, Tuya AI Coding comes with three core foundational capabilities: device connectivity, cloud services, and data intelligence. When users input a requirement, the AI does more than generate interfaces and interaction logic. It also automatically builds the full backend architecture, including databases, API gateways, user authentication, and device management, while directly connecting to Tuya's cloud infrastructure spanning more than 200 countries and regions. At the same time, Tuya AI Coding leverages Tuya's extensive AI hardware ecosystem, with native support for access to more than 100,000 SKUs. Foundational capabilities such as device management, data analytics, and weather information services can be added flexibly, enabling seamless integration between software applications and real-world hardware devices. Empowering Non-Technical Creators to Build AI Lifestyle Experiences Tuya AI Coding is designed primarily for creative users without technical backgrounds, including designers, product managers, entrepreneurs, freelancers, and students. For these users, the key needs in AI application development are clear: quickly turning ideas into working products, lowering technical barriers, validating concepts at low cost, and gaining a sense of creative achievement. Traditional development workflows, however, have long stood in the way. High technical barriers, limited resources, slow iteration cycles, and complex tools often prevent creative individuals from bringing their ideas to life. To address these challenges, Tuya AI Coding offers several core capabilities: Real-time preview and conversational iteration: During the generation process, the interface is rendered in real time, allowing users to refine details instantly through natural language commands such as "make the button larger" or "add dark mode." Template library and scenario-based support: Vertical use cases are supported with ready-to-use templates, making development more accessible and efficient. Cross-platform compatibility and one-click deployment: The platform automatically generates applications that work across PCs, smartphones, tablets, and other devices, while enabling one-click cloud deployment and easy social media platform sharing. A fully no-code workflow: What once took months in traditional development can now be compressed into minutes, lowering the technical barrier by 90%. As the AI industry undergoes a deeper shift in value creation, "unlocking creativity for everyone" is becoming just as important as improving efficiency. As more platforms begin to offer the ability to generate applications with a single sentence, Tuya AI Coding's differentiation becomes increasingly clear: it not only generates AI applications, but also enables those applications to integrate with Tuya's AI hardware ecosystem and accelerate real-world transformation. Tuya AI Coding is now officially available. Users can explore the platform at coding.tuya.ai . About Tuya Smart Tuya Smart (NYSE: TUYA ; HKEX: 2391) is a leading global AI cloud platform service provider dedicated to bringing AI into everyday life. Through its TuyaOpen open-source development framework and universal AI Agent engines, including the AI Agent development platform, Tuya integrates multimodal AI capabilities to lower barriers for AI development, efficiently advancing the realization of AI-driven lifestyles and accelerating AI integration with the physical world. Tuya offers innovative physical AI solutions for smart devices, commercial applications, and industry developers through its cloud computing and spatial intelligence capabilities. It also provides a complete, open, and neutral global AIoT ecosystem. This approach fosters a vibrant global developer community comprising brands, OEMs, AI agents, system integrators, and independent software vendors who collaborate to create smart solution ecosystems embodying the principles of sustainability, security, efficiency, agility, and openness. As of Mar 31, 2026, the Tuya AI Developer Platform had over 1,970,000 registered AI developers from more than 200 countries and regions. SOURCE Tuya Smart

title: NiSource Generation Company: A new name that reflects a proven customer-first strategy
summary:
As northern Indiana continues to attract significant economic investment and energy demand growth, one thing remains unchanged: our commitment to protecting customers while supporting the region's future.  

That's why NIPSCO Generation LLC is now NiSource Generation Company LLC (GenCo).  

The new name better reflects the company's role within the broader NiSource enterprise while clearly distinguishing it from NIPSCO's traditional utility operations. Importantly, this is a name change only, not a change in strategy.
body_text: As northern Indiana continues to attract significant economic investment and energy demand growth, one thing remains unchanged: our commitment to protecting customers while supporting the region's future. That's why NIPSCO Generation LLC is now NiSource Generation Company LLC (GenCo) . The new name better reflects the company's role in enabling this differentiated model that protects customers and promotes growth. Importantly, this is a name change only, not a change in strategy. Supporting Growth While Protecting and Benefitting Customers Through GenCo's structure, large-load customers, like data centers, pay for the generation and transmission infrastructure required to serve their needs. This approach helps ensure residential and local business customers are not responsible for funding infrastructure built specifically for new, high-demand users. In fact, the model charges these large-load customers for use of NIPSCO’s electric system and is expected to provide approximately $1.4 billion in direct bill credits to NIPSCO electric customers over the next 15 years , while strengthening the electric grid and supporting long-term economic growth across northern Indiana. Alignment with the Ratepayer Protection Pledge NiSource recently signed the White House's Ratepayer Protection Pledge, formalizing principles that have guided GenCo since its creation. The pledge is grounded in a simple idea: growth should pay for growth. New large-load customers should bear the costs associated with the infrastructure needed to serve them, helping protect existing utility customers from those investments. That same principle is at the core of the GenCo model. Before and after the transition to NiSource Generation Company, the company's purpose remains unchanged: support economic development, enable new growth opportunities and protect customers through a structure designed to maintain affordability. Building a Stronger Future for Northern Indiana Our GenCo model creates speed to market and helps develop a more resilient, future-ready grid, provides capacity needed to serve growing demand, and positions northern Indiana to compete for major economic development projects that bring jobs, tax revenue and long-term investment to the region. The name may be new, but the commitment is not. NiSource GenCo continues to reflect the principles that have guided the business from the beginning: Growth pays for growth. Growth is enabled with speed. Customers are protected. Customers benefit. And northern Indiana is positioned for the future. You can find more information about GenCo at the following resources: nisourcegenco.com

title: Best Swimming Pool Accessories to Elevate Every Swim
summary: Explore the top swimming pool accessories that make swimming safer, cleaner, and more fun. Learn which inground and above-ground pool accessories are must-haves for every pool owner.
body_text: If you’ve just purchased your dream pool and are waiting for installation to begin, now is a great time to think about which pool accessories can further elevate your space, transforming it into your own personal oasis. The best pool accessories make owning a pool a complete experience by balancing fun, safety, maintenance, and comfort. Whether it’s the colorful inflatable pool toys for a summer party or a reliable pool cover that keeps your backyard safe for kids and pets, we’re here to help you discover the best pool accessories for your backyard, so you have everything you need to enjoy peak swim season as soon as it begins. Why Pool Accessories Are Essential When most people think of pool accessories, inflatable floats and basketball hoops often come to mind. While these items can maximize the fun in your pool, accessories also include many of the items that keep your pool clean and safe to use. Accessories like robotic vacuum cleaners, water chemical monitors, safety fences, and covers are just as important as those for fun. For example, according to the American Red Cross, a four-sided isolation fence separating a pool area from the house and yard can reduce child drowning risks by 83% compared to regular fencing. Keep reading to learn about some of the best investments for pool accessories that prioritize safety, lower your maintenance commitment, and foster a beautiful, calming space you can enjoy for years to come. Best Pool Accessories for Every Pool Owner There are several top pool accessories that benefit every pool owner, regardless of the size, style, or material of your space. These items improve safety, maintenance, and overall enjoyment while balancing practical tools with fun add-ons. Some accessories are universal must-haves, such as covers and chemical test kits. Not only can these items keep your pool area safe and clean, they can also have year-round benefits. For instance, a pool cover can act as a thermal barrier that prevents evaporation, extending your season into cooler fall and spring months. Some of the top pool accessories include: Safety accessories like life jackets, safety covers, and pool fences. Maintenance items to keep pools clean, such as chemical test kits and skimmers. Fun accessories for poolside play, such as waterproof speakers and slides. Backyard upgrades for ultimate relaxation, such as umbrellas, coolers, and lounges. High-tech accessories that make pool ownership easier, such as chemical monitors and digital thermometers. Safety First: Accessories That Protect Swimmers Pool safety accessories are essential for maintaining a pool area that all of your loved ones can enjoy. They can give you greater peace of mind, knowing that your backyard is secure – especially for children and furry friends. Here are some of our top recommended safety accessories to keep your backyard pool-ready for all your friends and family: Life Jackets: A U.S. Coast Guard-approved, properly fitted life jacket is recommended for all children under five, as well as for those who are inexperienced or weak swimmers. Life jackets can be an irreplaceable safety accessory for young children, even if they are in the pool area without planning to enter the water, as they can act as an additional layer of protection in the event of an accidental fall into the pool. Pool Alarms: Pool alarms monitor for surface or pressure changes in your pool, which are usually caused by a person, pet, or object entering the water. These changes trigger the alarm, which can alert homeowners with either a loud siren or a notification on a smart device. These devices, especially when paired with a pool fence or cover, can provide multiple layers of protection for young children who might wander unsupervised into the pool area. Safety Covers: Safety covers stretch across the surface of your pool to create a physical barrier between the water and people or debris outside. There are a variety of different pool cover types, such as mesh nets and automatic covers that let you open and close your pool with a remote. Some areas, such as the state of Florida, have regulations about the type of pool cover that can be used on residential pools. Check with your pool dealer for more information on pool accessory compliance. Pool Fences: Pool fences wrap around the perimeter of your pool and often have self-latching gates that swing away from the pool and automatically latch behind you, leaving fewer opportunities for children to accidentally push them back open. Anti-Slip Mats: These mats are often made of high-friction materials that can provide wet surfaces around your pool with more traction. These accessories can be especially valuable in areas that are at a higher risk of becoming slippery when wet, such as ladders, stairs, and any patio area in the splash zone. Rescue Gear: Gear such as ring buoys, shepherd’s hooks, backboards, and a first aid kit can be essential for quickly pulling swimmers to safety and treating injuries in case of an accident around the pool. Keep It Clean: Maintenance & Pool Care Essentials You may already know that pool cleaning accessories are necessary for keeping your pool’s water clear and sparkling for the entire length of the season. However, they can also aid in making your pool more energy efficient, which can significantly cut down on your overall maintenance expenses. Check out some of the best maintenance accessories for keeping your pool clean and sparkling (with less work): Robotic Vacuums: These cleaners automate much of the scrubbing that would otherwise need to be manually done by homeowners. They can scrub pool floors and walls while also operating with their own filters, which can reduce wear and tear on your pool’s filtration system. Test Kits: Maintaining your water chemistry is the single most important factor in maintaining your pool and protecting your backyard investment. Test strips can help you quickly diagnose water imbalances that can cause bacteria and algae to form. Skimmers: Skimmers remove contaminants — like insects, debris, sunscreen, and body oils — that fall into your pool before they can begin to decompose. This filtration can help prevent your pool’s surface from unsightly stains. Solar Covers: These insulated covers help raise your water temperature and keep heat from escaping at night. They also prevent evaporation, as well as keep the sun’s powerful UV rays from disrupting chemical balances. This can significantly reduce your need for additional chemicals and maintenance treatments. Fun & Games: Accessories for Poolside Play Accessories like speakers, slides, and games are essential touches for any outdoor space, whether you’re creating an intimate personal oasis or hosting poolside for the whole block. Here are a few of our favorite additions for the party side of your pool: Waterproof Bluetooth Speakers: Play your favorite tunes while you swim laps in the morning or enjoy a pre-dinner cocktail poolside, without worrying about your speaker being in the splash zone. Pool Floats: These long floats allow you to be gently rocked by your pool water’s natural rhythm while you read, sip a cold drink, or work on your tan. Slides: For larger pool areas, a slide can transform your backyard into a true, everyday vacation spot. These accessories are especially popular with children of all ages and can add a resort-like quality to your space. Waterfall: Waterfalls add a natural elegance to your backyard, reducing outside noise and filling your space with tranquil, island-like sounds of cascading water. Pool Games: Games are excellent entertainment options that have mass appeal to adults and children . Many toys, such as inflatable animals and floats, can double as safety features, where children can have a designated place to rest in the water. Comfort & Style: Backyard Relaxation Upgrades The area surrounding your pool should be just as serene and beautiful as the pool itself. Whether you want to relax in the shade after work or host friends and family outdoors, here are some of our favorite relaxation upgrades: Patio Furniture: Patio tables and chairs can provide a comfortable and beautiful place for your guests to sit and relax while you grill or serve drinks poolside. Umbrellas: Umbrellas provide shade that can protect your skin from powerful UV rays. Use them to create a place out of the sun to catch up on your latest book club pick, or comfortably supervise children and pets in the pool. Ledges: Ledges are shallow areas that can serve as an ideal place for getting some sun or act as a more accessible and safe “splash pad” for young children. Loungers: These versatile and durable chaise lounges are designed to be a comfortable place to stretch out and relax. Coolers: Coolers keep cold drinks accessible in your pool area, meaning you no longer have to go in and out of the house when you want a drink. Keeping kids’ drinks handy in a cooler can also keep them from dripping water along entryways and inside, where pooling water can be a slip hazard. High-Tech Pool Accessories Your pool can now go digital with modern upgrades that make maintenance easier and more energy-efficient. Digital Thermometers: Water temperature is an essential factor for maintaining your chemical balance, as higher temperatures can cause chlorine to degrade. These tools can also help you confirm that heating equipment is functioning correctly during colder months. Smart LED Lighting: This lighting option uses less energy than incandescent bulbs, lowering your energy costs and extending the life of the bulbs. You can often change their brightness and color through an app on your smartphone, enabling you to change the mood of your pool with the click of a button. Robotic Cleaners: These cleaners automate much of the physical scrubbing and cleaning that would otherwise need to be performed manually. Chemical Monitors: Digital chemical monitors can give you real-time tracking for water quality factors like pH, sanitizer level, and temperature. They can send instant alerts to your smartphone when maintenance is needed, minimizing the guesswork of water balancing and preventing you from overusing chemicals. Solar-Powered Gadgets: Gadgets such as heaters, cleaners, and lights that use solar power can be more sustainable than electricity and can significantly lower your utility bill, especially for heating costs. The Attendant by Latham : This proprietary automation tool is a cloud-based system that gives you complete control over your pool from the convenience of your smartphone. Access settings that help you monitor climate control settings, temperature changes, water chemistry, pool lighting, and more with the click of a button. Best Accessories for Inground Pools Inground fiberglass and vinyl liner pools elevate your space from a backyard that’s identical to your neighbor’s to a luxury hideaway you can enjoy without leaving home. Pool accessories like tanning ledges, built-in lighting, and slides are durable features that meet the unique needs of inground pools while increasing your pool’s functionality and your home’s property value. Practical accessories like robotic cleaners, digital thermometers, and chemical monitors can be valuable investments in the health and beauty of your pool. These tools can help you catch maintenance needs in real-time, helping you keep your pool in the best condition possible without strenuous testing and extensive chores. Automatic pool covers, which can be fitted to inground pools during or after installation, are also excellent accessories for inground pools. Not only can they prevent evaporation, which can result in higher chemical costs, but they also provide a layer of security for friends, family, and pets in your pool area. Best Accessories for Above Ground Pools Because they aren’t installed fully in the ground, above ground pools need specific accessories to maximize your safety and comfort when enjoying them. These pools often need safe ladders or entry systems that are specially designed to accommodate the high sides of the pool. Because these ladders can become very slippery when wet, they should be fitted with anti-slip mats that help keep your loved ones safe as they enter and exit the pool area. Just like inground pools, above ground pools benefit from covers that help block the water from debris and UV rays. Solar covers are made from strong but lightweight material that prevents evaporation and raises the temperature of your pool by using power from the sun. This helps keep your water warm, especially during chilly nights in the spring and fall. Winter covers are also important for protecting your pool’s water from ice, snow, and rain, especially if you live in a cold climate. Because these pools often have less water volume, they need compact filtration tools that are designed to generate less pressure, as well as robotic cleaners designed to operate with less water flow. Smaller or portable pool floats and games can also be excellent additions to ensure that you can enjoy your above ground pool without feeling cramped. How to Choose the Best Pool Accessories for Your Needs Consider your pool’s unique needs and match them to the right accessories. You’ll also want to balance your budget with long-term value when considering seasonal and safety needs. For instance, an automatic pool cover can have a higher up-front cost than a mesh pool net, but it can also pull double-duty by enhancing the safety of your pool area and helping lower energy costs. You can also add other practical accessories like fencing, pool alarms, and water heaters to create layers of security and usability. This not only gives you a better return on investment by extending the length of your pool season, but it also prioritizes safety and comfort, especially for kids and pets. You should also consider lifestyle when you’re thinking about accessories. If you’re dreaming of long summer months spent relaxing in the sun, tanning ledges and pool floats can give you a dedicated place to catch some rays. If you love to entertain poolside, think about investing in patio furniture and umbrellas that can accommodate guests for a small, after-work happy hour, as well as big neighborhood barbeques. Find the Right Pool Accessories for Your Backyard Oasis Pool accessories are essential for safely enjoying your pool to the fullest while protecting the investment you’ve made in your home. When you’re thinking about the top pool accessories that are the best fit for your space, consider practical needs for maintenance and safety, but don’t forget those that will make your pool comfortable, beautiful, and fun for everyone enjoying your space. We’re Here to Help We’re here to help with pool advice, pointing you towards accessories that can make your backyard vision a reality. Contact us today to talk about the best accessories for your needs, whether you want to add features to an existing pool or design your space from scratch.
